Baseline inspected: `001490c14a6568972d16a663bb04c07a4255d30d`; governing supplement digest supplied by coordinator: `8f540171dd38711ad563459d1721277b84100b66a207379668f0efe6db8b208f`. All file:line anchors below were searched/read at this baseline and must be re-confirmed at build time. `bash scripts/deferrals-open.sh` returned no rows. Read root/docs/crates AGENTS, decomposition handoff, external decompose-spec skill, supplement §§0–2/5–6/9 and applicable Appendix A, E1/E2/E3, D3, F1/F3 source notes and relevant current owner code. No repository writes, runtime tests, providers, containers, installation, network task execution, branches or commits occurred. This memo is analysis, not evidence of product verification.

## Conclusion and Phase-3 boundary

The ratified supplement plus source notes provide enough authoritative semantics to author **full fixture engineering contracts**. I found no global design gap requiring decomposition to stop. R1/R2/R3 explicitly resolve the most important old alternatives (postterminal grade, first-valid selection, whole-vector reserve); do not revive E2 preterminal grading or E3's superseded parity fallback.

Existing APIs do NOT include `launch_bound`, `adopt_subject`, `plan_disposition_at`, `execution_settled` or `DurableEffectRef`. Those are cited proposed seams in E3 F1/F2/F4 and supplement §2, not already shipped public APIs. Their contracts may cite the names/semantics, but must not invent persisted event/class/domain names. The §9.3 amendment owner must specify/admit exact durable extensions using current owner codecs, ontology home and class table. This is an explicit prerequisite, not absent product design. An implementation-local Rust helper can be chosen routinely; a new persisted wire name cannot be silently frozen in the decomposition.

The genuine unresolved *inputs* are explicitly named gates: actual unchanged upstream task/oracle/runner/image and provider model/roles; shared HelperExecutor/Podman backend compatibility; exact supported bounds for the chosen provider; admissible clock continuity after restart; rights, access, recipients, actual retention dates, full archive quote and execution funding. Full fixtures can exercise these contracts with deterministic ports and typed refusal. Actual S1/S4/recipient/participant executions needing these choices must remain skeletons behind human/backend/resource gates. Never substitute LocalExecutor or a made-up task for failed backend admission. `cancel-async-tasks` is a source-note candidate, not a selected task.

One precise contract detail to carry into admission review: selection corrections are required to be authorized and append-only, but the supplement does not grant a new principal/role or new mutation endpoint. Reuse the existing authority model and have the ADR name the accepted authority proof and exact persisted revision schema; do not infer that any recipe caller may invalidate grades. Similarly, no public RPC adoption method, new receipt command, clock schema, transport cancellation guarantee or new backend has been authorized by the proposed Rust names.

## Proposed slices and unique primary ownership

Names X1… are local labels, not allocated ticket IDs. Each later branch forks from the immediately preceding ticket in the coordinator's full chain; DAG dependencies below are semantic predecessors. Primary REQ ownership appears once. “Support-only” means the ticket implements a named piece of a later owned requirement and cites that owner's acceptance; it does not create a second primary owner. This permits safe slices for E201/E207/E208 without turning those large requirements into oversized tickets. All acceptance below is deterministic E unless explicitly D or actual E/P execution. Core fixture slices are full contracts after cited architecture admission; exact gated executions are skeletons. Estimated focused read+edit working sets are 8–24k tokens, with 8–12k verification/review reserve; do not load entire 10k-line driver/service files.

### X1 — Durable launch binding and recoverable funding

Primary: support-only for **REQ-E-201** (primary at X2; aliases E-001/E-101 retained there). Depends: launch/grade ADR admission. Scope: experiment launch intent→slice→subject open→subject root allocation/binding→publish; recovery links or idempotently aborts/releases. Freeze required-grade/task/oracle/selection/instrument funding bindings before launch, but no grading producer yet. Proposed `launch_bound` is cited E3 F1/§2.1, not a new RPC. Likely working set: engine launch/reconcile and events/view, Account allocation API, ledger manifest/class/ontology registration only as admitted; experiment tests. 14–20k tokens + reserve.

Negatives: injected failure between each persistence step, stale claim, orphan root/slice, duplicate publication, conflicting bytes/identity, recovery without cross-run atomicity, second subject creation, root used before bind. Verify recovery returns identical subject/root or owned abort/release exactly once. AC-2-1, AC-2-3; consumer X2/X7/B2 and receipt population R3. Existing tests `engine.rs:669 lifecycle_next_claim_launch_settle_close`, `:724 launch_requires_a_live_claim`, `:1068 launch_refuses_insufficient_budget_and_stays_replannable`.

## Dependency and coupling checks for final plan

1. ADR contracts → X1 → X2 → X3 → X4; selection X6 can be parallel in DAG after ADR; X4/X6 → X5; X1/B2/X5/X6 → X7.
2. X1 → B1 → B2; X2/X4/B1/B2/T1 → B3; X2/X3 → T1; T1/B3 → T2. This avoids a T1↔B3 cycle: prepared call accepts the already-owned retained representation; T2 is final wire integration.
3. Owner producer contracts → R1; R1 + owner refs → R2; X7/B3/T2/R1/R2/analysis metadata → R3; R3 → R0/R4/R5; rights A1 can proceed with fixtures after R1/R2.
4. X3/B3/R3/backend gate → O1 → O2 → O3; retain fixtures vs actual trial dispositions. All execution/receipt inputs + gate → S1. R0/R4/A1 + participation authority → H-outside.
5. Do not merge X1–X7 into one P1: reading whole engine/open/service/driver/projection is ~20k lines before tests. Do not split shared selection per consumer. Do not merge B1/B2/B3/T1/T2 into one P6/P7; they share a clear prepared-call contract but separate lower-owner obligations. Do not create one receipt ticket touching every producer plus all recipient procedures; profile, enumerators and population join are real seams.
6. R0 lifecycle fix is independently landable, but its six recipient controls consume R2/R3 for the stronger profile claim. Allow early fix with owner/support trace rather than postponing harmless repair until collection.
7. All advertised procedures need direct negative tests after inaccessible producer stores. This is stronger than a bundle unit test and different from P participation evidence. Native closure does not validate oracle truth.
